newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UNICEF hails Britain's pledge to scrap mine stocks.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF hails Britain's pledge to scrap mine stocks.

text.p: The U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF) welcomed on Thursday a pledge by Britain's new Labour government to destroy its anti-personnel mines by 2005 and to press more vigorously for a worldwide ban.

"The steps announced by the government in London constitute a major breakthrough that can only help the Ottawa negotiations," UNICEF executive director Carol Bellamy said in a statement. She was referring to a process that began with a meeting in Ottawa last October of governments committed to a global landmine ban.

But, she added: "We should not let it blur the fact that the world continues to lose ground to these devices, which kill or main 6,000 to 8,000 children a year, shatter families, destroy livelihoods and subvert the best efforts of struggling people to better their lives."
Bellamy said more than 115 million unexploded mines remained in the ground, with that number growing by two million annually.
